published_prior_art.cite: gu2026optimally Appendix A.1 gives the closest fixed-class two-budget minimax display but leaves this asymmetric product-scale converse unmatched; jin2025hardnormal and jin2025sharp study different supplied-nuisance or ECC experiments.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Open-ended Question 1 / honest_scope
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The mean-zero fixed-class converse is the claim under review; its status as a strict tightening of Gu et al.'s literal Appendix A.1 lower display is assumed only if the authors confirm that E[epsilon Y|X,T]=0 is a typographical error.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: A product converse for m_PL^0 is a conditional claim on the explicitly defined mean-zero experiment; comparison as a strict tightening of gu2026optimally Theorem A.1 is conditional on source correction, otherwise it is a closely motivated distinct experiment.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 18–19, Appendix A.1, equations (A.1)–(A.2), Theorem A.1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Equation (A.1) literally imposes E[epsilon Y|X,T]=0, whereas equations (1.1) and (3.2) impose E[epsilon|X,T]=0; (A.2) has the fixed-class supremum/infimum/supremum order, and Theorem A.1 displays the stated upper minimum and lower expression.
The note states that optimality of black-box DML remains open even for the PLM coefficient and identifies variance as the unresolved distinction from structure-aware settings.

source_verification_receipts.version: Public NeurIPS 2025 author manuscript, arXiv:2507.02275v3, 7 November 2025
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 3.1 is a binary-treatment supplied-nuisance quantile-risk lower bound, while Theorem 3.2 is a known-constant-variance Gaussian-treatment barrier with a product term and logarithmic factor; neither is the fixed-class expected-absolute-risk experiment proposed here.
The PLM-restricted instantiation concerns expected conditional covariance and a PLM-preserving density perturbation family, rather than the partially linear coefficient minimax frontier.
The published article gives cross-fitted Neyman-orthogonal DML inference for the partially linear regression coefficient and its Robinson-style partialling-out score.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Publisher record; primary theorem text was inaccessible
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The publisher record verifies the cited Root-N-Consistent Semiparametric Regression article; no formula-level comparison with its inaccessible theorem text is used in this review.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Obtain an author correction, erratum, or archived source clarification for Appendix A.1, then promote the conditional comparison to an unconditional strict-tightening statement with the cited equation locator.
Specify a worked bounded non-atomic paired-cell family and its two fixed learner witnesses, including the affinity calculation target, so the fuzzy-hypothesis handle becomes directly executable.
Add a same-class upper-bound corollary for the mean-zero experiment, explicitly combining the DML product upper rate with the proposed converse to state a matched asymmetric minimax frontier.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 to attempt the fixed-class two-channel fuzzy-hypothesis construction, retaining the Appendix-A.1 comparison as conditional until source correction is obtained.
